courses.title: Media and Its Impact On Society
courses.description: This course provides an examination of the mass media's influence on culture, industry, and society globally. Students will explore the historical evolution of media systems, as well as their ongoing impact on politics, the economy, and daily life. The course also emphasizes media literacy, equipping students with critical skills to analyze and navigate information in an era of digital media. It addresses current challenges, including the role of AI in media, ethical dilemmas, and the complexities of truth and misinformation in the digital age.
courses.advisories: ENGL C1000 or ENGL C1000H or ESL D005.

Evaluate the role, power and influence of mass media industries in the U.S. and globally.

courses.title: News Writing and Reporting
courses.description: This course provides instruction and practice in reporting, along with the fundamentals of news writing for media. It includes analysis of typical news stories, with a concentration on the language and style of news writing. Students will focus on the organization and structure of news stories, the development of leads, and the basic story types, while gaining practical writing experience. The course is NOT part of the student news publication, La Voz News.

courses.title: Social Media Strategies for Journalists and Content Creators
courses.description: The course critically examines how journalists and news organizations use emerging forms of social media for news gathering, distribution, and audience engagement. This course also explores the ethical considerations and dilemmas inherent in social media reporting.

metadata.Student Learning Outcomes: Demonstrate ability to leverage social media as a powerful tool for communication, engagement, and influence. Demonstrate an understanding of the development of social media platforms and their impact on contemporary journalism. Demonstrate the ability to design and implement a comprehensive social media strategy for journalistic endeavors, integrating ethical considerations, practical skills, and audience engagement strategies. Practice the use of ethical and legal principles in reporting and writing for social media.

courses.title: Editorial Leadership for Student News Media
courses.description: The course provides practical, hands-on experience in planning, assigning, editing, and publishing print, video, and/or web content as members of the college newspaper, magazine, or media staff and editors. Students lead the production of non-fiction content with a focus on journalism, fostering student leadership and collaboration.

metadata.Student Learning Outcomes: Apply editing skills to news, feature and opinion pieces for a student-led print newspaper, broadcast and/or website following ethical guidelines and journalistic conventions. Develop leadership skills while assigning and working with peers (reporters and photographers and/or fellow editors) as they create content for student media. Develop a digital portfolio of work suitable for presentation on a news organization website or broadcast.

courses.title: Introduction to Public Relations
courses.description: This course explores the principles, history, development, and current professional practice of public relations. Concepts of planning and executing effective communication strategies, including message design and distribution, for any organization will be covered. Applicable journalistic writing styles are also covered.
courses.advisories: ESL D272. and ESL D273., or ESL D472. and ESL D473., or eligibility for ENGL C1000 or ENGL C1000H or ESL D005.

metadata.Advisory(ies): ESL D272. and ESL D273., or ESL D472. and ESL D473., or eligibility for ENGL C1000 or ENGL C1000H or ESL D005.
metadata.Student Learning Outcomes: Demonstrate knowledge of the history, role and function of public relations in today's society and global economy. Compare ethical and legal case studies and distinguish which of the chosen methods for handling the issues are best aligned with the Public Relations Society of America member code of ethics and media law. Research and design a public relations strategy for a specific entity and create a press release (using Associated Press style) and associated media strategy, based on a stated goal and means of evaluating outcomes.

courses.description: The course provides an introduction to multimedia storytelling with a journalism emphasis. Students will explore techniques including the use of video, photos, audio, animation, and text to create interactive news and feature stories for online platforms and electronic media. Additionally, the course covers basic journalism concepts such as ethics, law, critical thinking, research, and synthesis.
